Attackers Actively Probing for Upgrade-Window RCE Vulnerability in WordPress

WordPress 코어 4.7~7.1.3의 CVE-2026-119977은 코어 업그레이드 중 예측 가능한 임시 설치 경로를 통해 인증 없이 원격 코드를 실행할 수 있는 취약점이다. 악용은 짧은 업그레이드 시간에만 가능하지만, Wordfence는 관련 공격 시도 24만 건 이상을 차단했으며 CISA는 이 취약점을 KEV 목록에 추가했다. WordPress 7.1.4 또는 해당 버전 계열의 보안 패치로 즉시 업데이트하고, 업데이트...

https://www.wordfence.com/blog/2026/11/attackers-actively-probing-for-upgrade-window-rce-vulnerability-in-wordpress-core/

🚨 Your WordPress security update could be the exact moment an attacker compromises your website.

A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 8.1), exposes a dangerous TOCTOU race condition in the WordPress core update mechanism, potentially enabling unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE). Affecting WordPress versions 2.7 through 7.1.3, the flaw allows attackers to exploit the publicly accessible wp-content/upgrade/ staging directory, inject malicious PHP files during the update window, and turn a routine core upgrade into a potential server compromise. Even more concerning? Updating directly to WordPress 7.1.4 does not eliminate every transition-time exploitation scenario. The vulnerability is listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, with exploitation attempts observed in the wild. We break down the complete attack chain, TOCTOU mechanics, exploitation architecture, affected versions, indicators of compromise, and mitigation strategies, including Nginx and Apache hardening.

🔬 Technical breakdown: https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/cve-2026-119977-wordpress-update-race-condition-rce/

CVE-2026-6295.description: The WP Optimizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 's' parameter in all versions up to and including 2.5.0. This is due to an unsafe subquery-detection branch in the Query::parse_key_compare_field() method that, when the user-supplied value matches the regex ^[(\s]*SELECT\s+, wraps the value in parentheses and embeds it directly into the SQL string without any escaping or quoting. While the normal LIKE code path correctly uses esc_sql($wpdb->esc_like(...)) and wraps the value in single quotes, this branch completely bypasses those protections. Because the attack payload (SELECT ...) contains no single quotes, WordPress's wp_magic_quotes() provides no protection. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with administrator-level access to inject arbitrary SQL subqueries — including time-based blind payloads — that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

posts.content:
AI Agents Are Getting Powerful. What Can They Do For You?

The AI agent market has officially entered the awkward teenage years.
The demos are impressive. Agents can browse the web, send email, fill out forms, write documents, book travel, run code, manage files, and operate software that doesn’t even have an API.
They can also do things you absolutely did not intend them to do.

That is the part of the story that gets considerably less screen time.

Over the last year, we went from “AI that answers questions” to “AI that can actually do stuff.”
OpenClaw, Muse, Grok Bot, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT Work, Gemini Spark, Manus and Hermes Agent all take slightly different approaches to the same fundamental problem:

How much autonomy are you willing to give software that can act as you?

And that turns out to be a much more interesting question than which model scores highest on a benchmark.

The new AI benchmark is blast radius

For years, we compared AI models on intelligence.

Presentations.
Websites.

Your agent is a dependency.
If an agent is deeply embedded in your workflow, what happens when its pricing changes?

Or the company disappears?
Or your credits expire?
Agent portability is going to become a real enterprise concern.

Your time isn’t.

The rule I would use for every AI agent

Regardless of which agent you choose, I would start with three rules.

1. Give it a separate account – Just like a new employee in your company.

Don’t give an experimental agent access to your primary Gmail, your company’s production environment or your entire Google Drive. Create a sandbox.

2. Start read-only.

Let the agent observe before you let it act. Reading a calendar is one thing. Canceling appointments is another. Reading email is one thing. Sending email as you is another.

3. Make the first tasks reversible.

Have it organize files. Research something. Draft a document. Find information.
Don’t start with:
“Here are my credentials. Run my company.”

It apparently isn’t.

It’s going to be about who can safely give software more autonomy. That’s a much harder engineering problem. An LLM generating bad text is annoying.

An agent sending the wrong email is embarrassing.
An agent leaking your credentials, deleting production data, purchasing something expensive or falling for a prompt injection is an incident. And as agents become more capable, the distinction between “AI feature” and “employee with a laptop” starts to disappear.

That’s why I’m paying less attention to agent benchmark scores and more attention to boring things like:

  • Where does it run?
  • What is the security boundary?
  • What credentials does it get?
  • What happens when it is compromised?
  • Can I stop/undo it?
  • Can I take my data and move somewhere else?

Those questions aren’t nearly as sexy as a demo where an AI books your entire vacation.
But they are the questions that will matter when the agent is running your business at 2:00 AM.

The future of AI agents isn’t just about making them smarter.
It’s about making them safe enough to let them work while we’re asleep.

CVE-2026-25253.description:
## Summary

The Control UI trusts `gatewayUrl` from the query string without validation and auto-connects on load, sending the stored gateway token in the WebSocket connect payload.

Clicking a crafted link or visiting a malicious site can send the token to an attacker-controlled server. The attacker can then connect to the victim's local gateway, modify config (sandbox, tool policies), and invoke privileged actions, achieving 1-click RCE. This vulnerability is exploitable even on instances configured to listen on loopback only, since the victim's browser initiates the outbound connection.

## Details

The root cause is the lack of validation for `gatewayUrl` combined with auto‑connect behavior on page load. With the change users now need to confirm the new gateway URL in the UI.

## Impact

This is a token exfiltration vulnerability that leads to full gateway compromise. It impacts any Moltbot deployment where a user has authenticated to the Control UI. The attacker gains operator-level access to the gateway API, enabling arbitrary config changes and code execution on the gateway host. The attack works even when the gateway binds to loopback because the victim's browser acts as the bridge.

CVE-2026-59105.description: Jumis (formerly Tildes Jumis) creates and uses a Microsoft SQL Server login named ##Tilde_JumisAdmin## whose password is derived deterministically from a single non-secret input - the SQL Server name (@@servername). The derivation algorithm is hard-coded in the client application and is identical across every installation; it contains a hard-coded secret key for entropy. Because the only input (the server name) is not secret - the instance suffix is hard-coded and the host name is discoverable via the SQL Server Browser service (UDP 1434), the TDS pre-login response, or DNS/NetBIOS - any party able to reach a Jumis SQL Server can compute the password offline and authenticate. The ##Tilde_JumisAdmin## login is a member of the sysadmin server role. Successful authentication therefore grants full administrative control of the SQL Server instance and read/write access to every customer's accounting database hosted on it. The on-premise server installation also programmatically enables xp_cmdshell during routine operation, so sysadmin access escalates to operating-system command execution on the database server.

CVE-2026-107622.description: The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.5 via a form-type confusion attack through the `bf_post_type` parameter. This is due to the public frontend submission handler `buddyforms_form_response_no_ajax()` authorizing logged-out submissions based solely on the target form's `public_submit` flag while independently trusting the attacker-supplied `$_POST['bf_post_type']` to determine the post type of the newly created object — a cross-check introduced in 2.10.2 applies only to existing posts (`post_id != 0`) and is completely bypassed for new-object creation — combined with the `save_post` listener `buddyforms_edit_form_save_meta_box_data()` lacking both a `current_user_can()` capability check and a form-builder nonce, causing it to unconditionally persist attacker-supplied `$_POST['buddyforms_options']` for any newly inserted `buddyforms` CPT post. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert a rogue BuddyForms form configuration with an attacker-controlled `new_user_role` value into the live global form registry, then submit a registration through that form to create a new WordPress account with administrator-level privileges and achieve full site takeover. Exploitation requires the WordPress site to have "Anyone can register" enabled and at least one public BuddyForms form attached to a page, both of which are standard BuddyForms deployment configurations.

CISA added Apple vulnerability CVE-2024-27834 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports that Russian state-sponsored group APT29 is chaining it with WebKit flaws to steal browser cookies. The "Poisoned Source" campaign uses watering hole attacks and a supply chain compromise to target unpatched iOS and Android devices.

**Update all your Apple devices now (iOS 18.7.3 or later, macOS Sonoma 14.5 or later, Safari 17.5 or later), and your Android phones too, because hackers are breaking into unpatched phones when you simply open an infected website. If you think you may have been exposed, sign out of all your important accounts on every device and watch for strange activity, because the stolen browser cookies let attackers get in without your password or MFA code.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #attack #activeexploit
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/cisa-warns-of-active-exploitation-chaining-apple-webkit-and-pointer-authentication-flaws-9-m-e-k-2/gD2P6Ple2L

This issue is fixed in Safari 17.5, iOS 16.7.8 and iPadOS 16.7.8, iOS 17.5 and iPadOS 17.5, macOS Sonoma 14.5, tvOS 17.5, watchOS 10.5. An attacker with arbitrary read and write capability may be able to bypass Pointer Authentication.

CVE-2026-116624.description: The Advanced Members for ACF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.0 via the `acf[_amem_local_user_password]` parameter of the `[advanced-members-account-password]` shortcode form submission. This is due to a PHP operator-precedence bug in the `pre_update_value` function of `acf/fields/class-user-password.php` that assigns boolean `true` instead of the resolved user ID to `$user_id`, causing the `_can_edit()` authorization check to pass for any logged-in user via PHP loose equality, and causing `wp_update_user()` to cast `'ID' => true` to integer `1` — unconditionally targeting the primary administrator account. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the password of user ID 1 (the site's primary administrator) with an attacker-chosen value, granting full administrative access to the site. The intended exclusion guard in `Account::process` that strips the password field before saving is defeated because `amem_save_all_fields()` re-reads the full field list from `amem()->submission` and silently overwrites the caller-supplied excluded fields array with an empty array, ensuring the password field is always processed.

Zyxel GS1900 Switches Compromised via Zero-Day RCE

Zyxel patched a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-107441) in GS1900 switches after attackers exploited it to deploy rootkits on nearly 1,000 devices.

**Make sure the management interface of your Zyxel GS1900 switches can’t be reached from the internet and is open only to trusted admin networks, then update the firmware to version 2.90(Axxx.3)C0 or later. The June 2026 patch does not stop this attack, so check your switches for any connections to the 981666[.]xyz domain. If you find one, treat the switch as compromised and factory reset it before you update it.**

The Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK provides TypeScript client and server implementations of the Model Context Protocol. From 2.0.0 until 2.3.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/server, applications that shared one stateless HTTP transport or one Mcp...

#CVE #vulnerability #infosec #cybersecurity #security #Tenda #patchstack

CVE-2026-111770.description:
### Summary
In affected versions, an MCP server reached over HTTP could deliver one client's responses and notifications to another client. This happened when clients shared one stateless transport, or one `McpServer` or `Server` instance.

Messages were matched to a connection by JSON-RPC `id` alone. SDK clients number requests from 0, so ids collide in normal use.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if more than one client can reach your HTTP endpoint and your code creates the transport or the server once at startup, instead of once per request or per session. Until this release, the README examples of `@modelcontextprotocol/hono`, `express`, `fastify` and `node` showed that pattern.

Affected versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.0.0 through 2.2.0.

Not affected:

- `createMcpHandler()` with a factory that builds a new server on every call
- stdio servers
- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.26.0 and later

### Fix
Upgrade to `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.0 or later.

**You also need to change your code.** The SDK now refuses to be shared, so an affected app fails requests after upgrading: a second `connect()` rejects with `ALREADY_CONNECTED`, and a stateless transport rejects its second request.

Change to one of these:

- **`createMcpHandler()`:** pass a factory that builds a new `McpServer` on every call.
- **Per request:** build a new `McpServer` and a new transport inside the request handler.
- **Per session:** set `sessionIdGenerator` and keep one `McpServer` and one transport per session.

If you cannot upgrade yet, the same change fixes affected versions.

CVE-2026-111768.description: The Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK provides TypeScript client and server implementations of the Model Context Protocol. From 1.3.0 until 1.32.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and from 2.0.0 until 2.3.0 in @modelcontextprotocol/server, HTTP servers did not enforce a limit on the number of array elements and object keys validated in one request. The affected surface is validation of HTTP requests containing arrays or object keys. The trigger is an array-element or object-key validation workload large enough to exhaust memory while remaining within the request size limit. A single request within the default 4 MiB limit can terminate the process with JavaScript heap exhaustion. No credentials are required unless the application authenticates before SDK processing. Tools accepting arrays or records carry the greatest risk. stdio-only servers do not expose the HTTP request path. Upgrading alone does not enable the new validation bound. Operators must configure both a tool-input element bound and an appropriate request body size limit. This issue is fixed in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0 and @modelcontextprotocol/server 2.3.0.

CVE-2026-83374.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Security).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u503, 8u503-perf, 11.0.32.1, 17.0.20.1, 21.0.12.1, 25.0.4.1, 27;    Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20.1 and  21.0.12.1;   Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19.1.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.9 (Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N).
